Resolves #18284
Related: #18303 #18309 #18293

🌿 Two roots that happen to spell their workspaces the same way can no longer meet in one drag: the coordinator now asks who may commit before it asks who is underneath, and a bare id has stopped meaning home.

A cross-window drag resolves its target among the zones registered under the source's `sortGroup`, and two Workstation roots on one App-Worker heap register identical stable identities (`workstation-main`, the vessel ids) under that one group — so a drag from root A could claim root B's surface, preview into it, and commit into B's document through the "local" branch, because the payload's bare workspace id equalled the target's. This PR adds the second axis ADR 0029 §2.3 now names: **ownership**, the topology Group of the window a surface renders for, declared by the surface and read at claim time. `sortGroup` keeps answering *are these protocol-compatible?*; ownership answers *may these share one commit authority?*; the two are never concatenated.

`Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` admits candidates by ownership before the claim pass, the hit-test, the preview and any embodiment — `admitsOwnership(source, target)` on two opaque strings, dock-blind — and both legacy first-intersecting doors (pointer and native) obey the same admission. A non-admitted zone never claims, and it releases only a claim it holds itself, so equal stable identities from two roots never meet in one arbiter. Because ownership is read live, the winner is revalidated against this pass's admission before it is returned: a target whose Group turns foreign or unresolved while its claim is still live stops previewing at the next pass, a remaining same-Group candidate takes over, and the arbiter's `release` now takes the holder so a zone leaving the claim set can never take another zone's claim with it. A source that declares nothing (the header sort zone) drags under the surface registered for its own window in the same group (`resolveSourceOwnership`) — registry identity, not dock semantics. Two tiers, as the amended AC-7 requires: `undefined` is outside the Group world and meets only undeclared surfaces (the `draggable/dashboard/SortZone` consumers keep today's namespace); a declared `null` is participating but unresolved and matches nothing.

On the dock side, `window/DragTarget` gains the `resolveOwnershipId` owner seam behind a live `ownershipId` getter (never `undefined`: every dock surface declares); `window/Participation` resolves it from its workspace's Group by default or from the host's seam, forwards it to its target, stamps `dockSourceOwnershipId` beside `dockSourceWorkspaceId` on the native path, and re-checks it first thing in `commitDrop`, so an unstamped payload or another Group's payload commits nothing even when its bare workspace id equals this one's. `interaction/TabSortZone` stamps the same field at drag start from the coordinator's answer. The three hosts declare: Workstation and DemoB pass their Group, the cross-window witness harness registers window A's own surface as a real dock window would.

Evidence: L2 achieved, plus a contract-level browser witness → L3 required (criterion 10 of #18303's closeout matrix asks for preview and staging absence observed in a second full root, with a same-Group positive control). L2: the composed four-participation unit arm. The witness — `examples/dashboard/crossWindowWitness`, a real browser App Worker driving the real coordinator and real participations, with injected window rects and a stubbed hit-test — runs one gesture that first crosses a second root's popup carrying the same bare workspace ids under another Group (no preview, no staged embodiment, no commit, its documents byte-identical afterwards) and then commits exactly once into root A's own target; `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockCrossWindowWitnessNL.spec.mjs` asserts every one of those readings. Residual, with its exact owner as the matrix requires for its L3 rows: the rendered observation — a tab dragged from one full Workstation root over a second full root's window, read in that root's own DOM — is #18379, blocked by #18376 and recorded by the epic's author in #18303's criterion-10 row (a second full root kills the first root's renderer: its OffscreenCanvases are driven by the shared App Worker in the first root's process). Close target: #18284's own acceptance criteria are met at L2 plus the witness; the parent's criterion-10 receipt stays open on #18379.

## Deltas from ticket
**The Workstation native resolver stamps at `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:1175`, not `:1154`** — the line the ticket's ledger names had drifted by the time this branch was cut; the site is the same statement (`pane.dockSourceWorkspaceId = Workspace.MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID`).

**A header sort zone does not declare ownership itself; it drags under its window's registered surface.** The ticket's ledger reads the stamp sites as the places ownership is written, and they are — but the value comes from `DragCoordinator#resolveSourceOwnership`, because a projected `sortZoneConfig` is clone-safe and carries no closures, and a string frozen at projection time could not be "read at claim time" for a host that learns its Group later. The registered participation for the zone's window is that live reader.
